scope: Proposition 4.1 (Endpoint control) of the manuscript “GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs” (preprints/GOE-bulk-universality-for-fixed-degree-random-regular-graphs-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 219 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d8e092ab0484f8b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a deterministic ξ > 0, depending only on d, E, with the following property. For every fixed k ≥ 1 and D > 0, there are constants Ck,D < ∞ and yk,D < ∞ such that, for every fixed s ∈ R and every fixed y ≥ yk,D, lim sup n→∞ P ( |mn(s + iy) − m∗| + ∥Mn,k(s + iy) − Kk(m∗)∥ > y−ξ ) ≤ Ck,Dy−D . (4.2) The limit is through admissible graph sizes. The constants and the height threshold are independent of s; the argument s + iy is fixed before taking the limit.
